Building WebAssembly (WASM) providers

Build a small Rust component that publishes JSON to Moonframe, then read it from a Luau view and send it messages. This guide is for people writing a provider by hand and coding agents building one for an app.

A provider supplies data; a mod draws it. A provider in providers/counter/ publishes as app.counter, and mods address it as provider:counter. Moonframe runs each WASM provider in its own sandbox with Wasmtime. You do not rebuild or restart the Moonframe executable to add one.

Choose a provider kind

Need Kind
Transform data, keep an in-memory model, or use a host capability wasm
Publish a sample JSON file without running code static
Run a CLI, read files, make HTTP requests, or reuse a Python/Node program process
Use the host app's Rust libraries or asynchronous services directly native

WASM providers cannot read your files, use the network, inherit your environment, or spawn processes. Today the only machine-data capability is system (CPU, memory and network counters). There are no http, fs or exec capabilities. Process and native providers run with the user's access instead. See the library guide for native providers.

Rust is the path Moonframe builds automatically. Other languages work if they produce a WebAssembly Component Model component implementing the same WIT interface; a plain core WASM module is not enough.

Set up the folder

You need Moonframe with its default wasm feature enabled, Rust/Cargo, and the WASI Preview 2 target:

rustup target add wasm32-wasip2

Use a current stable Rust toolchain (the example uses edition 2024). In the Moonframe repository, use its pinned rust-toolchain.toml.

Choose the folder that already holds your app's main.luau:

Working on App folder
The cloned starter or an app on the Rust library app/ in that project
A profile made with moonframe app new The profile project root
Your installed Moonframe ~/.config/moonframe (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/moonframe)

For an installed app, write to the user's folder, not inside the signed application bundle. In the commands below, run from this app folder. Pick an unused provider name: a user provider replaces a built-in provider with the same folder name. Names use lowercase a-z, digits, - and _.

Create this layout:

providers/counter/
  provider.toml
  Cargo.toml
  src/lib.rs
  wit/provider.wit
mods/wasm-counter/
  main.luau

mkdir -p providers/counter/src providers/counter/wit mods/wasm-counter

Copy wit/provider.wit from the Moonframe version you are using into providers/counter/wit/provider.wit. In a cloned starter, from app/:

cp ../wit/provider.wit providers/counter/wit/provider.wit

For a separate project, obtain that file from the matching Moonframe release tag or commit. Keep a local copy in the provider so it builds wherever its folder is copied. WIT is the interface definition shared by the component and the host; do not invent or change its exports.

Declare the provider

Write providers/counter/provider.toml:

kind = "wasm"
interval = 1.0
capabilities = []

[settings]
initial = 0

The folder name determines app.counter, not the Cargo package name. Manifest fields for a WASM provider are:

Field Meaning
kind Must be "wasm"; no command or file field.
interval Seconds to wait for a message before calling tick; defaults to 1.0, allowed range 0.1–3600.0.
start "on-demand" (default), or "always" to start with the app.
capabilities An empty list by default; currently only "system" is supported.
[settings] Your configuration, converted to JSON and passed to start.

Unknown manifest fields are errors. Keep provider-specific configuration under [settings].

Write providers/counter/Cargo.toml:

[package]
name = "counter"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
publish = false

[lib]
crate-type = ["cdylib"]

[dependencies]
serde_json = "1"
wit-bindgen = "0.63"

[profile.release]
lto = true
opt-level = "s"
strip = true

[workspace]

The empty [workspace] makes this an independent crate, even inside the host's Rust workspace. Keep the generated Cargo.lock in source control. Leave the library filename at its default: Moonframe locates the output using the package name, replacing hyphens with underscores.

Implement the component

Write providers/counter/src/lib.rs:

use std::cell::RefCell;
use serde_json::{Value, json};

wit_bindgen::generate!({ path: "wit/provider.wit", world: "provider" });

struct Counter;

#[derive(Default)]
struct State {
    initial: u32,
    count: u32,
}

thread_local! {
    static STATE: RefCell<State> = RefCell::new(State::default());
}

fn snapshot(state: &State) -> String {
    json!({ "count": state.count }).to_string()
}

impl Guest for Counter {
    fn start(settings: String) -> Result<(), String> {
        let settings: Value = serde_json::from_str(&settings)
            .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
        let initial = match settings.get("initial") {
            None => 0,
            Some(value) => value.as_u64()
                .and_then(|value| u32::try_from(value).ok())
                .ok_or("initial must be an integer from 0 to 4294967295")?,
        };
        STATE.with_borrow_mut(|state| *state = State { initial, count: initial });
        Ok(())
    }

    fn tick() -> Option<String> {
        Some(STATE.with_borrow(snapshot))
    }

    fn receive(message: String) -> Option<String> {
        let message: Value = serde_json::from_str(&message).ok()?;
        STATE.with_borrow_mut(|state| {
            if message.get("add").and_then(Value::as_bool) == Some(true) {
                state.count = state.count.saturating_add(1);
            } else if message.get("reset").and_then(Value::as_bool) == Some(true) {
                state.count = state.initial;
            } else {
                return None;
            }
            Some(snapshot(state))
        })
    }
}

export!(Counter);

wit-bindgen generates the Guest trait and export! macro from the WIT file. Implement all three exports:

Export Called when Result
start(settings) Once per component instance, before the first tick Ok(()), or Err(message) to fail startup.
tick() Immediately after startup, then after each interval without a message Some(json) publishes a snapshot; None keeps the previous value.
receive(message) A mod sends a message to the provider Some(json) publishes immediately; None keeps the previous value.

Frequent messages can postpone periodic ticks: interval is an idle timeout, not a fixed-rate timer. Keep work bounded and return promptly.

Each publication replaces app.counter; it is not a partial merge. Return the whole object the views need. JSON objects become Luau tables, arrays become lists, and null becomes nil. Publications are limited to 1 MiB of JSON, 10,000 values and nesting depth 16 (the root is depth 0). Invalid JSON or a component trap stops the provider and reports a problem.

Messages contain the payload alone. The button below sends {"add":true} to receive, not a {"from":...,"message":...} envelope. That envelope belongs to process providers. WASM's current interface does not expose the sender or provide native-provider reply routing; publish results for views or provider/counter subscribers to consume.

The STATE value survives calls, but resets when the provider restarts or reloads. It is not saved between app launches. Use a mod's persisted state for UI choices that should survive quitting.

Draw it and send messages

Write mods/wasm-counter/main.luau:

return mod {
    region = "right",
    view = function(state, app)
        local counter = app.counter
        if not counter then
            return ui.text "Waiting for the WASM counter…"
        end
        return ui.panel {
            title = "WASM counter",
            ui.column {
                ui.text(`Count: {counter.count}`),
                ui.button { "Add one", to = "provider:counter", msg = { add = true } },
                ui.button { "Reset", to = "provider:counter", msg = { reset = true } },
            },
        }
    end,
}

The starter shell places mods from the right region automatically. A custom shell must include that region or mount wasm-counter explicitly. Handle app.counter == nil while the component builds or before it publishes its first value.

Reading app.counter from a drawn view starts the provider on demand. Subscribing to provider/counter or sending a message also starts it. Once started, it keeps running even if the view is hidden. Use start = "always" only when it should work before any mod needs it.

Build, run and check

From the app folder, compile the exact component:

cargo build --release --target wasm32-wasip2 \
  --manifest-path providers/counter/Cargo.toml \
  --target-dir target/providers

The output is target/providers/wasm32-wasip2/release/counter.wasm. This target produces a component; wasm32-unknown-unknown does not produce the required artifact. You do not need cargo component for this example.

Check and run using the command for your app:

App Validate UI and manifests Open the app
Cloned starter (from repository root) just check and just types just run
Linked profile moonframe --profile NAME --check moonframe --profile NAME
App on the library (from Rust project root) cargo run -- --check cargo run
Installed starter with user mods moonframe --check moonframe

--check does not compile or execute WASM providers. A passing check validates the manifest and Luau but is not a runtime test. Build the component too, then verify in the running app:

  1. The panel shows Count: 0 (or your configured initial).
  2. Add one updates the count immediately; Reset restores initial.
  3. Changing initial in provider.toml restarts this provider with the new value.
  4. Editing src/lib.rs rebuilds it; a compile error shows as a provider problem.

Agents should report which checks they ran and which runtime interactions still need the user's verification.

When Cargo.toml and Cargo are available, Moonframe builds the source automatically on startup and when the provider's folder changes. Builds go to the app's cache (the starter uses ~/.cache/moonframe/providers, or its $XDG_CACHE_HOME equivalent). Only the changed provider restarts; the window and other providers keep running. Changes to dependencies outside the provider folder may require a manual reload.

A failed source build is an error, even if an older provider.wasm exists. Without source or without Cargo, Moonframe loads provider.wasm from the provider folder instead. If neither path is available, startup fails.

Host calls and limits

To log a diagnostic, use the generated host interface:

moonframe::provider::host::log("counter started");

This moonframe module comes from wit-bindgen, not a dependency on the Moonframe Rust library. Logs go through the host's logging system; run the app from a terminal to inspect them. Publishing happens through the return value of tick or receive, not println!.

For machine load, put capabilities = ["system"] at the top level of provider.toml, before [settings], then call:

let sample = moonframe::provider::host::system_load()?;
let load: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&sample)
    .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;

This fragment belongs in a function returning Result<_, String>. Without the capability the call returns an error. cpu and memory are fractions from 0 to 1; memory_used and memory_total are bytes, and received and transmitted are bytes per second. See the complete system provider for collecting a bounded history and handling a failed host call.

Each component has a 64 MiB aggregate linear-memory cap and a fresh fuel budget per call (currently 2 billion Wasmtime fuel units, not a wall-clock deadline). Bound histories, collections and computation accordingly. There are no preopened directories or inherited environment variables; adding a crate does not grant access to the machine.

The running component is sandboxed; the build is not. Cargo runs as the user. Moonframe refuses provider/local-dependency build scripts, build-dependencies, .cargo folders and toolchains named by path, and builds outside the provider's directory. Proc macros and published dependencies' build scripts can still execute during compilation. Review source and dependencies before building a provider from elsewhere.

Package and share

For source development, keep provider.toml, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, src/ and the local wit/ together. Other developers need Rust and the wasm32-wasip2 target.

For a prebuilt distribution, the runtime needs only:

providers/counter/
  provider.toml
  provider.wasm

Copy the built counter.wasm to the literal filename provider.wasm in a separate staging folder beside its manifest. Leave Cargo.toml out of that staged folder so machines with Cargo do not rebuild it. Keep your development sources. The component is portable across the platforms supported by the matching Moonframe host interface.

In the cloned starter, just stage stages the built-in app/ with its WASM providers prebuilt; just bundle uses that staging step. For an app on the library, cargo run --release -- bundle also packages its WASM providers. See building and bundling apps for profile bundles.

Git packages installed with moonframe app install or moonframe mod install are source-only: they reject binary files, including provider.wasm. Ship source through those commands; prebuilt components belong in bundled releases or manually staged app folders. Do not include target/ or compiled components in a source package.

Troubleshooting

Symptom Check
Nothing builds; app.counter stays nil Is the mod drawn, and does its view read app.counter? Does the shell place its region? Check the provider banner and terminal log.
Cannot find std for the target Install wasm32-wasip2 for the toolchain actually building the provider.
Cannot find the WIT file The macro path is relative to the provider crate root. Keep wit/provider.wit inside it.
Missing exports or component instantiation error Use wasm32-wasip2, the matching WIT, all three Guest methods and export!(Counter).
Source build fails despite a provider.wasm Source takes precedence when Cargo is available; fix the build or use a separate prebuilt-only staging folder.
start: initial must be… Fix [settings] initial; a start error prevents the first tick.
Invalid JSON, memory error or fuel exhaustion Return valid, bounded JSON and limit work per call; inspect the provider's error.
system_load returns an error Put capabilities = ["system"] before [settings].
No data in a custom library app Ensure its wasm Cargo feature is enabled; without it providers publish nothing and report the disabled feature on a message.

Coding-agent recipe

When asked to build a WASM provider:

  1. Identify the app folder and choose an unused provider name. Confirm that WASM's available capabilities cover the task.
  2. Copy the matching WIT locally; create an independent cdylib crate with kind = "wasm". Keep manifest keys separate from [settings].
  3. Define the published JSON shape and accepted message payloads before writing the view. Validate settings and handle unknown messages.
  4. Implement start, tick, receive and export!. Publish whole snapshots, bound work and memory, and do not assume runtime state persists.
  5. Read app.<name> with a nil fallback; send payloads to provider:<name>. Follow the Moonframe and component skills for UI.
  6. Build for wasm32-wasip2, run the app's headless checks and Luau type checks where configured, then verify startup, a message and reload. State explicitly when an interactive check was not performed.
  7. Keep source packages and prebuilt release staging distinct. Link to this guide instead of duplicating a different provider protocol.

Further examples: system uses the host capability; Gantry telemetry keeps a larger in-memory model and handles messages (its data is simulated).
